Looking at the trace, the temperature has been remarkably steady around 27–28 °C through the morning, with a single 1 °C rise to 29 °C at 13:00 — the first time it has reached that value. The wind has been persistently southerly, mostly 12–19 kt, which at this station and season is effectively the sea breeze direction, and that tends to cap daytime heating. The dewpoint is high (25–26 °C), so any further warming would require mixing out that moisture, which the strong onshore flow argues against.

It is now 13:00, and at this latitude in mid-June the climatological peak is typically around 14:00–15:00, though the sea breeze often caps it earlier. The 29 °C reading is new but only 1 °C above the flat morning plateau, so it is plausible that 29–30 °C is the ceiling under this regime. The cloud cover has been present all day (SCT), but not thickening into a clear convective shutdown; still, with the sea breeze established and steady, substantial additional heating is unlikely.

Given the strong marine influence, the late hour relative to the typical sea-breeze onset, and the modest diurnal range so far, the most likely outcome is that 29 °C holds or gains at most 1 °C more. A 2 °C rise would require a late break in the sea breeze or a significant clearing, which the observations do not suggest; 3+ °C is very unlikely.
